open_points.subject: A03 runner protocol validity
open_points.text: “distinguishes a valid runner channel from an invalid complete message” and “runner_channel_invalid”
open_points.question: What exactly makes the runner channel valid, what constitutes a complete message, and which malformed, truncated, extra, or out-of-order messages count as an invalid complete message rather than an absent returned message?
options: Define a closed runner-message schema and framing; any received complete message that fails it is invalid, while EOF without a complete message is absent
Treat any channel framing or message defect as runner-channel invalid
Leave protocol validation to the sandbox implementation
open_points.default_guess: Use a closed framed-message schema: a fully framed message that fails schema validation is runner_protocol_failed; clean EOF without one is an ordinary crashed execution.

open_points.subject: A03 protocol-failure outcome precedence
open_points.text: “Outcomes are closed and checked in this order, the first that holds deciding: wall deadline passed — timeout; a limit hit — resource_exhausted; … crashed” versus “a complete runner message is invalid, output is discarded, the execution is recorded crashed with detail runner_protocol_failed”
open_points.question: If an invalid complete runner message is observed in an execution that also passes its deadline, hits a resource limit, or records a sandbox trap, which outcome wins?
options: Apply rule 5 precedence, so timeout, resource exhaustion, or sandbox violation can win over the protocol failure
Runner protocol failure overrides every ordinary execution outcome
Protocol failure overrides only crashed and contract_violation
open_points.default_guess: Apply the published rule 5 precedence, using runner_protocol_failed only when no earlier outcome holds.

open_points.subject: A03 simultaneous cleanup and protocol failure
open_points.text: “If cleanup cannot be confirmed, or a complete runner message is invalid, output is discarded, the execution is recorded crashed with detail cleanup_failed or runner_protocol_failed respectively”
open_points.question: Which detail is recorded when the complete runner message is invalid and cleanup also cannot be confirmed?
options: cleanup_failed wins
runner_protocol_failed wins
Record both details
Define the combination as a separate detail
open_points.default_guess: cleanup_failed wins because failure to confirm cleanup is the stronger containment failure.

open_points.subject: M07 TrialExecution detail_code
open_points.text: M07 says “detail_code: … cleanup_failed … value_too_large … none otherwise”, while A03 requires a TrialExecution to be recorded crashed with detail “runner_protocol_failed”
open_points.question: Can a trial execution carry runner_protocol_failed, and if so is it a new M07 detail_code or some other field?
options: Add runner_protocol_failed to M07 detail_code
Do not persist runner_protocol_failed on TrialExecution
Represent it in a separate diagnostic field

open_points.subject: A04 admission interrupted by runner protocol failure
open_points.text: A04 says admission “never stops early — save for an execution whose cleanup cannot be confirmed” and records no verdict only for that case, while A03 test 12 says an invalid complete runner message “cannot produce an admission verdict” and stops the kernel
open_points.question: Must runner_protocol_failed stop admission without a verdict just like cleanup_failed, or may admission finish and record a refused verdict before the kernel stops?
options: Stop admission immediately and record no AdmissionVerdict
Finish the corpus and record a refused AdmissionVerdict before stopping
Record the failing TrialExecution, skip remaining cases, and record a partial refusal
open_points.default_guess: Stop admission immediately after recording the crashed TrialExecution and record no AdmissionVerdict.

open_points.subject: A03 enclosing request and shutdown sequence
open_points.text: “the sandbox result requires the kernel process to stop after that record is written” and “the response is flushed before the kernel process stops”
open_points.question: After recording runner_protocol_failed, what response and additional state changes are allowed before shutdown—for an explicit try, an implementation submission, a run advancement, and startup recovery—and must run status, waiting points, dependants, or admission state be updated before the response is sent?
options: Return the recorded crashed execution, make no further advancement or verdict changes, flush that response, then stop
Return internal_error after recording the execution, flush it, then stop
Complete normal enclosing run or admission bookkeeping before returning and stopping
During startup recovery stop without a surface response, but define separate behavior for request-triggered executions
open_points.default_guess: Record only the crashed execution, make no admission verdict or further run advancement, return an internal-error response when a surface request exists, flush it, and stop; startup recovery stops without a response.
